implementation_summary: Replaced the placeholder `test.skip(true, 'S1 skeleton — body lands in S6')` body in `e2e/tests/multi-user-md.property.spec.ts` with the real fc.assert property-test wiring. The 13-command arbitraries array uses `fc.constant` for no-arg commands and `fc.tuple` + `.map` for device-parameterised commands (sharing the same arbDevice = `fc.constantFrom<Device>('A1', 'A2', 'B')`). Per-run setup seeds a fresh `ModelStateMD` with `cachedPubkeyA` and `cachedPubkeyB`, calls `fc.asyncModelRun`, then `real.quiesce()`, then the five assertion functions. The `void (USER_B_NPUB as string)` suppression was also removed since `USER_B_NPUB` is consumed directly by `InCommand_MD`. The test title was updated from `[A15,C0]` to `[A15,C0,S5,S6,S10]` to reflect the full invariant set now wired.

tests_added.note: The property test replaces the placeholder. Count remains 1 test x 3 projects; the body is now real (was previously skip).

key_decisions: Used `fc.tuple(arbDevice, arbTitle, arbDesc).map(...)` for CtCommand_MD and similar multi-arg commands to ensure fast-check's shrinker can minimise each argument independently.
Used `fc.tuple(arbDevice, arbNewName).map(...)` for RdCommand_MD — avoids closure capture of arbNewName.
arbDevice declared locally inside the test body, distinct from the 2-party file's arbActor (type Device vs ActorId).
No identity-restore step at end-of-run: MD has no SwCommand_MD so pubkeyA never changes (architecture.md constraint 11).
Test title updated from [A15,C0] to [A15,C0,S5,S6,S10] to match the assertions now wired.
void (USER_B_NPUB as string) suppression removed — symbol is consumed by InCommand_MD which is defined in the file.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: The spec says to use `arbDevice.map(...)` for device-parameterised commands, but `CtCommand_MD` and `UtCommand_MD` also require string arguments (`title`, `desc`). The spec pseudocode at lines 239-247 shows placeholder comments (`/* + arbTitle/arbDesc */`) without specifying whether to use `fc.tuple` or a nested `.chain`. The 2-party reference file (lines 1052-1064) uses `fc.tuple(arbActor, arbTitle, arbDesc).map(...)`, making the intended pattern clear — but that required reading the reference to resolve the gap in the spec.
retrospective.surprised_by: The `void (USER_B_NPUB as string)` suppression at the file's end was left from S1 as a placeholder for a symbol not yet used. After S1–S5 `InCommand_MD` was implemented and directly imports/uses `USER_B_NPUB`, so the suppression became dead code. Removing it as part of S6 was correct per the story spec ('Trim S1's void(...) unused-import suppressions if any remain') but the suppression did not actually suppress an unused import — the symbol was already live. This was a no-op correctness fix, not a regression risk.
